sections.heading: C — Speed limits, work zones, emergency vehicles and school buses
sections.markdown:
## C — Speed limits, work zones, emergency vehicles and school buses

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Replace any child safety seat that has been in a crash, and know that with a secondhand seat you may not be notified of a recall. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
Michigan law makes it illegal to leave a child under 6 alone in a vehicle when the length of time or the circumstances create an unreasonable risk of harm or injury. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
Leaving a child in the vehicle with a supervisor aged 13 or older who is not legally incapacitated does not violate that law. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Never leave children or pets alone in a vehicle; teach children a vehicle is not a play area, lock it when parked, and keep keys out of their reach. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
Vehicle sensors decide whether an air bag deploys based on the type and severity of a crash, and air bags may sit in the steering wheel, dashboard, roof columns or doors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Seat belts stay the best protection in rollover, side impact and rear-end crashes, so buckle up even when the vehicle has air bags. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
Parents are encouraged to seat all children 12 and younger in the back seat to avoid air bag injuries in a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
Drivers should keep at least 10 inches between the center of the breastbone and the center of the steering wheel. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
A pregnant rider should wear the lap belt over the hips rather than the stomach, the shoulder belt across the chest, and sit as far from the air bag as possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A01
Michigan's Basic Speed Law requires a careful and prudent speed for conditions that lets you stop within the clear distance ahead, never above the posted limit and sometimes below it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A01
The standard limit is 15 mph in mobile home parks and some municipal parks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A01
The standard limit is 25 mph in platted subdivisions and condominium complexes, while limits in business districts, parks, and school and hospital zones vary, so watch the signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A01
A work zone is 45 mph when posted that way; if not posted for 45 mph, the area's normal limit applies. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A01
Unless another limit is posted, non-freeway streets and all highways are 55 mph. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A01
Freeways carry a 70 mph maximum and 55 mph minimum unless posted otherwise. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A01
School buses and trucks are held to 65 mph on freeways, and to 55 mph on freeways whose limit is below 70 mph. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A01
Construction, maintenance and work area warning signs are diamond-shaped with black letters on an orange or yellow background. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A02
Work zone signs can mean part of a lane, a whole lane or the entire road is closed, or that work is happening beside the road, on shoulders or in ditches. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A02
A construction zone may last a short time or one or more seasons, and advance signs warn you before you reach it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A02
Construction workers may direct traffic in a work zone, and you must follow them even when their directions conflict with a traffic control device. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A02
Most construction, maintenance or surveying zones are 45 mph unless posted otherwise, and some return to the normal limit when no workers are present. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A02
Fines double for every moving violation in a work zone. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A02
Speeding in a work zone costs three points for 10 mph or less over the limit, four points for more than 10 up to 15 mph over, and five points for more than 15 mph over. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A02
Injuring or killing someone in a work zone can bring fines up to $7,500 and up to 15 years in prison. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A02
Where lanes merge in a construction zone, white-and-orange barrels and signs mark the merge, and you follow the signs on when and how to merge. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A02
Merge strategies and traffic patterns can differ by project and change as work progresses, so watch barrels, signals, markings and workers' hand signals. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A02
State and local road agencies may add flashing or oscillating green lights to maintenance vehicles, used only during road work; when you see them, slow down and drive with caution. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A02
Private contractors may not display green lights, which were chosen because the eye is most sensitive to green, making them visible farther away in snow or dust. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A03
Yield to emergency vehicles approaching from any direction with red and blue lights, and to stopped emergency vehicles showing red, blue or amber lights. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A03
Authorized emergency vehicles include ambulances, fire and police vehicles, and private vehicles of firefighters or life-support agency members when authorized. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A03
Emergency-use vehicles of federally recognized nonprofit charities and clearly marked road service vehicles such as tow trucks with red or amber lights also count. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A03
For a stopped emergency vehicle, slow to at least 10 mph below the posted limit and move over a lane if you safely can; if not, slow down and leave as much room as possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A03
Breaking the move-over law for authorized emergency vehicles is a civil infraction, rising to a felony if emergency personnel are injured or killed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A03
Breaking it around other authorized vehicles, such as garbage trucks, utility trucks and road maintenance vehicles, is a misdemeanor. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A03
When an emergency vehicle approaches with red and blue lights and a siren, pull to the edge of the road clear of intersections, stop, and stay until it passes, watching for more. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A03
Keep your foot on the brake while stopped so the brake lights show emergency drivers you have stopped. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A03
Stay at least 500 feet behind a moving emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren, and never pass it unless its driver or a police officer directs you to. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A03
Stop at least 20 feet from a school bus showing flashing red overhead lights, because it is loading or unloading passengers. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A03
No stop is required for a school bus across a divided highway when a barrier, such as a concrete or grass median or an island, separates the two directions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A03
Failing to stop for a school bus brings double the normal moving violation fine, with higher fines and possible jail if someone is hurt or killed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0042]
